entries.title: The gig economy and digital payments
entries.description: The growth of the “gig” economy could have far-reaching implications for payment systems. Gig work involves digital platforms that intermediate between workers and (retail or business) customers, in areas as diverse as ride-hailing and food delivery, freelance design and professional services, and customer service.

entries.title: MaRCo@BIS: AI-agentic econometric analysis for central bankers
entries.description: This paper introduces MaRCo@BIS, the MAcroeconometric Research Companion: a framework of plain-text workflow files, a verified dictionary of canonical model specifications and a tested reference library, read by an off-the-shelf agentic coding environment.

entries.title: Ready-to-run  global  liquidity  stress tests for banks and banking  systems
entries.description: Liquidity risk remains a persistent threat to financial stability, as starkly demonstrated by the 2023 banking turmoil in the United States and Europe. Hence, the ability to quickly gauge banks’ liquidity risks could prove useful especially during periods of market stress, but also to assess differences in liquidity buffers across peer economies and banks.

entries.title: US monetary policy, macroeconomic news and the global secular decline of interest rates
entries.description: The global secular decline in long-term interest rates since the 1990s has been largely driven by cumulative yield changes during U.S. monetary policy announcement windows (FOMC windows).

entries.title: Gaining (and losing) currency: a global database of currencies, 1850-2026
entries.description: Over the past two centuries, officially issued currencies have become firmly en trenched as a nearly universal institution in economies around the world. But the path to this arrangement has not been smooth: currencies have come and gone, in line with political changes, periods of hyperinflation or currency reforms and, in some cases, entry into currency unions.

entries.title: Scenarios for future banking: implications for profitability, liquidity and solvency
entries.description: Who will perform banking’s core functions a decade from now, and how will risks and profitability evolve? Our framework structures expert judgement rather than forecasts.

entries.title: Prewar US business cycles under uncertainty: reconstructing quarterly GDP before 1947
entries.description: Official quarterly US GDP estimates begin in 1947; earlier quarterly histories must be reconstructed using annual benchmarks and historical indicators. To investigate uncertainty in these reconstructions, this paper systematically compares specifications drawn from the literature for reconstructing quarterly GDP during 1919–1946. The comparison evaluates predictions on concealed postwar quarters and separates variation across specifications from coefficient uncertainty within a model.

entries.title: Building AI on credit: structures and spillovers
entries.description: Capital expenditure to build artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure is growing fast, and a rising share is financed with long-term debt and through complex off-balance sheet arrangements.

entries.title: Chokepoints in global supply chains: lessons from rare earths and hard disk drives
entries.description: Concentration and limited substitutability can turn the efficiency gains from global supply chains into vulnerabilities. However, the consequences of chokepoints depend on their underlying nature.

entries.title: News shocks and inflation:  theory and evidence from  large oil discoveries
entries.description: We study how news shocks affect inflation in open economies, using large oil and gas discoveries with realized production lags of at least five years as observable news about future output. Panel local projections show that discoveries raise core consumer prices over the subsequent decade, with about half the increase occurring prior to extraction.

entries.title: AI Kill Switches: What Policymakers Should Know
entries.description:
Policymakers have recently proposed requiring “AI kill switches” to quickly stop an AI system or limit the impact of a harmful or unwanted AI incident. This piece describes different potential implementations of AI kill switches at each layer of the AI stack and offers key takeaways for policymakers. 
 The post  AI Kill Switches: What Policymakers Should Know  appeared first on  Center for Security and Emerging Technology .

entries.title: Espionage, AI, and the Risks of Strategic Overreaction
entries.description:
Allegations involving Nvidia’s chief executive have renewed scrutiny of Chinese intelligence collection and U.S. controls on advanced AI chips. Meanwhile, local resistance to data centers—a sentiment that’s been linked to PRC influence campaigns—raises a different challenge to the infrastructure supporting American AI leadership. Although these episodes are not evidence of a coordinated Chinese campaign, together they illustrate how external security threats and domestic policy choices can shape the U.S.–China AI competition—and why responses must be grounded in evidence. 
 The post  Espionage, AI, and the Risks of Strategic Overreaction  appeared first on  Center for Security and Emerging Technology .

entries.title: Spy scandal highlights contradictions at heart of Trump’s China policy
entries.description:
CSET’s Sam Bresnick shared his expert insight in an article published by The Washington Post. The article examines how allegations of Chinese espionage involving Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang have raised questions about President Donald Trump’s approach to U.S.-China relations, semiconductor export controls, and national security. 
 The post  Spy scandal highlights contradictions at heart of Trump’s China policy  appeared first on  Center for Security and Emerging Technology .

entries.title: The phantom life of Alice Huang, alleged Chinese spy who had affair with Nvidia CEO
entries.description:
CSET’s Sam Bresnick shared his expert insight in an article published by The Washington Post. The article examines allegations of Chinese espionage involving Alice Huang, her relationship with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, and concerns over U.S. semiconductor export controls. 
 The post  The phantom life of Alice Huang, alleged Chinese spy who had affair with Nvidia CEO  appeared first on  Center for Security and Emerging Technology .

entries.title: The U.S.–China AI Competition: Two Paths to Artificial General Intelligence
entries.description:
The United States leads the world in frontier AI models and computing, but China is pursuing broader paths toward artificial general intelligence, including robotics, “embodiment,” and brain-inspired systems. A forthcoming CSET study compares the two countries’ strengths and asks what U.S. policymakers may miss when they treat AI competition as a single race. 
 The post  The U.S.–China AI Competition: Two Paths to Artificial General Intelligence  appeared first on  Center for Security and Emerging Technology .

entries.title: How Black-Box Distillation Works
entries.description:
This piece overviews how black-box distillation works in practice to inform proposed legislation and ongoing policy debates around adversarial distillation. We consider how adversarial distillation from proprietary U.S. models may have occurred at each step of the process and highlight areas of uncertainty around the methods Chinese labs employed. We also consider the potential impact of that distillation on China’s AI development. 
 The post  How Black-Box Distillation Works  appeared first on  Center for Security and Emerging Technology .

entries.title: Pentagon AI oversight office struggles to keep pace with department’s ambitions, GAO finds
entries.description:
CSET’s Owen J. Daniels shared his expert insight in an article published by Military Times. The article examines a Government Accountability Office report highlighting staffing shortages, incomplete initiatives, and oversight challenges as the Pentagon accelerates its adoption of artificial intelligence. 
 The post  Pentagon AI oversight office struggles to keep pace with department’s ambitions, GAO finds  appeared first on  Center for Security and Emerging Technology .

entries.title: China’s Next Frontier
entries.description:
CSET’s Kathleen Curlee and Sam Bresnick shared their expert analysis in an op-ed published by Foreign Affairs. The article examines China’s rapidly expanding commercial space industry and military space capabilities, exploring how advances in reusable rockets, satellite constellations, and counterspace technologies are challenging U.S. space superiority.  
 The post  China’s Next Frontier  appeared first on  Center for Security and Emerging Technology .

entries.title: AI & Tech Brief: Jay Clayton takes control
entries.description:
CSET’s Owen J. Daniels shared his expert insight in an newsletter published by The Washington Post’s WP Intelligence. The article examines President Donald Trump’s appointment of Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton to lead the new “Super Intelligence Force” and its implications for U.S. AI policy. 
 The post  AI & Tech Brief: Jay Clayton takes control  appeared first on  Center for Security and Emerging Technology .

entries.title: Should We Track AI Chips?
entries.description:
CSET’s Jacob Feldgoise, Kyle Miller, and Hanna Dohmen dove deep into investigating how location verification methods can—and cannot—improve enforcement of export controls on powerful AI chips, culminating in their report. I sat down with Jacob to learn more about the issue, their findings, and what those findings mean for mitigating AI chip smuggling. 
 The post  Should We Track AI Chips?  appeared first on  Center for Security and Emerging Technology .
